title: Interactor
body:
"Interacts with objects or structures within the world. Requires permissions from the user."

The Interactor is a logic component that can be purchased from Alan's AutoLogistics. It is used to interact with objects.

Functionality

The Interactor interacts with a neighboring object. While the Interactor itself is a 1×1×1 object, the probe on the front of the Interactor adds an additional 1.75 stud range that allows it to interact with an object. As of June 2025, the Interactor ability is depends on the region it controls. Players can change the size, postion of the region (merged into Size mode in Build Mode) to wherever they wanted - allowing to remote control various logics. All interactable items that hit or included in the region, will receive same output signal.

The Interactor will activate a single time whenever the signal level changes, and this behavior may need to be accounted for when using activation devices such as the Commander.

Interacting with the size buttons on machines like the Forge or Planker acts as if the player was pushing the button a single time. This means that the Interactor will need to be pulsed multiple times if the user wants to automate selecting a size for their machines.

Conveyors like Straight Conveyors or Intersection Conveyors can have their directions switched with an interactor. A signal of 5 turns off the conveyor, less than 5 sets the conveyor to the default direction and more than 5 sets the conveyor to reverse. Note that, since interactors activate when the input signal changes, you must use a constant signal to toggle conveyors; a switch or slider will send a constant signal, while a button sends a pulse that then changes back to zero. The slider is the best choice for this as it requires no other logic to set up, while a switch needs 3 number interfaces, 3 relays, and 3 switches.

A signal of 10 allows you to respawn vehicles, signal of 15 allows you to change the vehicle type, and a signal of 20 despawns vehicles. A Number Interface can be used to control this.

With Elevator, a signal between 0 and 10 will decide the length ratio of the Elevator - 0 for normal deactivated state, 10 for fully extended state. This allows player to do multiple flooring using the same elevator. Signal larger than 10 (more specifically, 20) will deactivate the Elevator.
